Significant Accomplishments and Conclusions Topic Area 1 – Systems Analysis of Chemical Recycling Plastic Infrastructure A central outcome was the development of integrated multi-scale modeling and optimization frameworks that combine experimental data from multiple sources and scales (e.g., molecular simulations, lab experiments) with rigorous process modeling, supply chain modeling, techno-economic analysis, and life-cycle assessment. These frameworks enabled consistent benchmarking across solvent-based recycling, thermochemical upcycling, and material recovery pathways. Its application showed that solvent-based STRAP processes can recover polymers at costs comparable to virgin resins, even for complex waste streams, and identified process configurations that offer clear environmental advantages. A key product of our research is a family of process models (implemented in the Python- based package BioSTEAM) for applications to multiple industrially relevant waste streams, including disposable face masks, biomanufacturing plastics, and printed multilayer films. These process models can be readily adapted for solvent-based recycling for any other post-industrial waste, which will help inform practical process design choices in future systems of interest. These models can also be used to develop educational materials and case studies for process design courses. Our research has also generated open-source models and data for conducting diverse studies associated with plastics upcycling. In parallel, optimization-based and LLM-based waste stream classification and routing approaches were developed to connect collection, sorting, and conversion decisions at the infrastructure level.
